exercises.why_bg: На английски: on a bus, on a train, on a plane, но in a car и in a taxi.

exercises.sentence: He's waiting ___ the door.
exercises.why: 'At' marks a point rather than a space you are inside.
exercises.why_bg: „At“ бележи точка, не пространство, в което си.

exercises.sentence: You can see the new logo ___ the picture.
exercises.why: Things are in a picture in English. 'On the picture' is a direct translation.
exercises.why_bg: На английски нещата са „in a picture“. „On the picture“ е буквален превод.

title: Prepositions of Time and Transport
rule_en: Use AT for exact times (at 9, at noon), ON for days and dates (on Monday, on 5 May), and IN for longer periods (in June, in 2024, in the morning). For transport, use BY with no article: by bus, by train, by plane — except "on foot".
rule_bg: AT за точен час (at 9, at noon), ON за дни и дати (on Monday, on 5 May), IN за по-дълги периоди (in June, in 2024, in the morning). За транспорт: BY без член: by bus, by train, by plane, с изключение на „on foot“.

form.label: at — clock time
form.value: at 9 o'clock · at noon · at the weekend

form.label: on — day or date
form.value: on Monday · on 5 May

form.label: in — month, year, season
form.value: in April · in 2019 · in the summer

form.label: by — transport, deadline
form.value: by train · by Friday

examples.en: The meeting is at 9 on Monday in June.
examples.bg: Срещата е в 9 часа, в понеделник, през юни.

examples.en: I go to work by bus, not by the bus.
examples.bg: Ходя на работа с автобус, без член пред „bus“.

examples.en: We'll finish it by Friday, not until Friday.
examples.bg: Ще го приключим до петък (краен срок), не „until“, което значи до тогава непрекъснато.

exercises.sentence: The meeting is ___ 9 o'clock.
exercises.why: 'At' for clock times. 'On' for days and dates, 'in' for months and years.
exercises.why_bg: „At“ за час. „On“ за дни и дати, „in“ за месеци и години.

exercises.sentence: Her birthday is ___ 5 May.
exercises.why: 'On' for a specific date or day of the week.
exercises.why_bg: „On“ за конкретна дата или ден от седмицата.

exercises.sentence: I usually travel ___ train.
exercises.why: Transport takes 'by': by train, by car, by bus. 'With the bus' is a word-for-word translation.
exercises.why_bg: Транспортът е с „by“: by train, by car, by bus. „With the bus“ е буквален превод.

exercises.sentence: We were both born ___ the same year.
exercises.why: 'In' for years, months and seasons.
exercises.why_bg: „In“ за години, месеци и сезони.

exercises.sentence: Please send it ___ Friday at the latest.
exercises.why: 'By' means not later than that moment. 'Until' means the action continues up to it, which is something else.
exercises.why_bg: „By“ значи не по-късно от този момент. „Until“ значи действието продължава дотогава, което е друго.

title: Prepositions After Verbs and Adjectives
rule_en: Some verbs and adjectives are always followed by the same preposition: depend ON, married TO, listen TO, look forward TO, interested IN, good AT. Learn each one as a single phrase, not word by word.
rule_bg: Някои глаголи и прилагателни винаги вървят с един и същ предлог: depend ON, married TO, listen TO, look forward TO, interested IN, good AT. Учи ги като цял израз, не дума по дума.

form.label: verb + preposition
form.value: depend on · answer (no to) · discuss (no about)

form.label: adjective + preposition
form.value: interested in · good at · married to

form.label: fixed
form.value: look forward to + -ing

examples.en: It depends on the client, not of the client.
examples.bg: Зависи от клиента, не „depends of“.

examples.en: She's married to a doctor.
examples.bg: Омъжена е за лекар.

examples.en: I look forward to hearing from you.
examples.bg: С нетърпение очаквам да чуя от вас.

exercises.sentence: It depends ___ the weather.
exercises.why: 'Depend' always takes 'on'. 'Depends of' comes straight from Bulgarian.
exercises.why_bg: „Depend“ винаги е с „on“. „Depends of“ идва директно от български.

exercises.sentence: He's married ___ an engineer.
exercises.why: In English you are married to a person, never with them.
exercises.why_bg: На английски човек е женен „to“ някого, никога „with“.

exercises.sentence: I'm really interested ___ this offer.
exercises.why: 'Interested in' is fixed. Note the -ed form: you are the one who feels it.
exercises.why_bg: „Interested in“ е устойчиво. И е -ed форма: ти си този, който го изпитва.

exercises.sentence: She's very good ___ negotiating.
exercises.why: 'Good at' for a skill, and the verb after it takes -ing.
exercises.why_bg: „Good at“ за умение, а глаголът след него е с -ing.

exercises.sentence: I look forward ___ your reply.
exercises.why: 'Look forward to' is fixed, and that 'to' is a preposition, so a verb after it takes -ing: looking forward to hearing.
exercises.why_bg: „Look forward to“ е устойчиво, а „to“ тук е предлог, затова глагол след него е с -ing: looking forward to hearing.

title: Verb + -ING or Verb + TO
rule_en: Some verbs are followed by -ing: enjoy, finish, avoid, suggest, mind, keep. Others take 'to': want, need, decide, hope, agree, offer, plan. A few take either with the same meaning: start, begin, continue. After a preposition the verb always takes -ing: 'interested in working', 'before sending'. There is no rule behind the lists, they have to be learned.
rule_bg: След някои глаголи идва -ing: enjoy, finish, avoid, suggest, mind, keep. След други идва „to“: want, need, decide, hope, agree, offer, plan. Няколко приемат и двете с еднакво значение: start, begin, continue. След предлог глаголът винаги е с -ing: „interested in working“, „before sending“. Зад списъците няма правило, трябва да се научат.

form.label: verb + -ing
form.value: enjoy · finish · avoid · suggest · mind · keep

form.label: verb + to
form.value: want · need · decide · hope · agree · offer · plan

form.label: either
form.value: start · begin · continue

form.label: preposition + -ing
form.value: interested in working · before sending

examples.en: I enjoy working with them, and I'd like to continue next year.
examples.bg: Харесва ми да работя с тях и бих искал да продължа догодина.

examples.en: She suggested meeting on Thursday, but I need to check my calendar.
examples.bg: Тя предложи да се срещнем в четвъртък, но трябва да проверя календара си.

examples.en: We finished reviewing the contract before sending it.
examples.bg: Приключихме с прегледа на договора, преди да го изпратим.

exercises.sentence: I enjoy ___ with this team.
exercises.why: 'Enjoy' is always followed by -ing.
exercises.why_bg: След „enjoy“ винаги идва -ing.

exercises.sentence: We decided ___ the offer.
exercises.why: 'Decide' takes 'to'.
exercises.why_bg: „Decide“ иска „to“.

exercises.sentence: She suggested ___ the meeting.
exercises.why: 'Suggest' takes -ing, even though the Bulgarian translation uses 'да'.
exercises.why_bg: „Suggest“ иска -ing, въпреки че българският превод е с „да“.

exercises.sentence: I'm interested in ___ more about the role.
exercises.why: After a preposition the verb always takes -ing.
exercises.why_bg: След предлог глаголът винаги е с -ing.

exercises.sentence: He offered ___ me a lift.
exercises.why: 'Offer' takes 'to'.
exercises.why_bg: „Offer“ иска „to“.

title: Verb Patterns That Trip Up Bulgarian Speakers
rule_en: "Agree" and "feel" are already complete verbs — never add "am" or "myself": I agree (not I am agree), I feel good (not I feel myself good). You SAY something, but you TELL someone something. After modal verbs like must, can, will, use the bare verb with no "to".
rule_bg: „Agree“ и „feel“ вече са пълни глаголи — не се добавя „am“ или „myself“: I agree, I feel good. Казваш нещо (say something), но казваш на някого (tell someone). След модални глаголи (must, can, will) глаголът е без „to“.

form.label: tell + person
form.value: tell me · tell him the price

form.label: say + no person
form.value: say something · say it to me

form.label: modal + bare verb
form.value: must finish (never must to finish)

form.label: no reflexive
form.value: I feel good (never I feel myself good)

examples.en: I agree with you.
examples.bg: Съгласен съм с теб.

examples.en: Can you tell me the price?
examples.bg: Можеш ли да ми кажеш цената?

examples.en: I must finish this today.
examples.bg: Трябва да го довърша днес.

exercises.sentence: I ___ with your plan.
exercises.why: 'Agree' is a full verb on its own. 'I am agree' comes from the Bulgarian 'съгласен съм'.
exercises.why_bg: „Agree“ е самостоятелен глагол. „I am agree“ идва от „съгласен съм“.

exercises.sentence: Can you ___ me the address?
exercises.why: 'Tell' takes a person straight after it: tell me, tell him. 'Say' does not: say something to me.
exercises.why_bg: „Tell“ иска човек веднага след себе си: tell me, tell him. „Say“ не иска: say something to me.

exercises.sentence: He ___ me that he'd be late.
exercises.why: There is a person right after the verb, so 'told'.
exercises.why_bg: Веднага след глагола има човек, значи „told“.

exercises.sentence: I ___ finish this by five.
exercises.why: Modal verbs take the bare infinitive. 'Must to' is never correct.
exercises.why_bg: След модалните глаголи няма „to“. „Must to“ никога не е вярно.

exercises.sentence: I ___ good about the decision.
exercises.why: 'Feel' needs no reflexive pronoun in English. 'Feel myself' is a direct translation of 'чувствам се'.
exercises.why_bg: „Feel“ не иска възвратно местоимение. „Feel myself“ е буквален превод на „чувствам се“.

title: Phrasal Verbs: Where the Object Goes
rule_en: Some phrasal verbs can be split: 'turn the light off' and 'turn off the light' are both fine. But when the object is a pronoun it has to go in the middle: 'turn it off', never 'turn off it'. Others never split: 'look after the children', never 'look the children after'. Which verb is which has to be learned, but the pronoun rule has no exceptions.
rule_bg: Някои фразови глаголи се разделят: „turn the light off“ и „turn off the light“ са еднакво правилни. Но когато допълнението е местоимение, то задължително отива по средата: „turn it off“, никога „turn off it“. Други не се разделят никога: „look after the children“, никога „look the children after“. Кой глагол от кой вид е, се учи, но правилото за местоимението няма изключения.

form.label: separable
form.value: turn the light off · turn off the light

form.label: with a pronoun
form.value: turn it off (never turn off it)

form.label: inseparable
form.value: look after them · deal with it

form.label: three parts
form.value: look forward to it · put up with it

examples.en: Can you fill in the form? Fill it in before you leave.
examples.bg: Може ли да попълниш формуляра? Попълни го, преди да тръгнеш.

examples.en: I'll look after the client while you're away.
examples.bg: Ще се погрижа за клиента, докато те няма.

examples.en: We need to deal with it today, not next week.
examples.bg: Трябва да се справим с това днес, не другата седмица.

exercises.sentence: Here's the form. Please fill ___.
exercises.why: A pronoun always goes in the middle of a separable phrasal verb.
exercises.why_bg: Местоимението винаги е по средата на разделим фразов глагол.

exercises.sentence: Can you turn ___?
exercises.why: A noun can go on either side. A pronoun can never go after the particle.
exercises.why_bg: Съществителното може и от двете страни. Местоимението никога не може след частицата.

exercises.sentence: I'll look ___ while you're away.
exercises.why: 'Look after' never splits.
exercises.why_bg: „Look after“ никога не се разделя.

exercises.sentence: We have to deal ___ today.
exercises.why: 'Deal with' is inseparable, so the object stays after the preposition.
exercises.why_bg: „Deal with“ е неразделим, затова допълнението остава след предлога.

exercises.sentence: She turned ___ because the salary was too low.
exercises.why: A noun can sit in the middle or at the end. 'Down it' is never possible.
exercises.why_bg: Съществителното може да е по средата или накрая. „Down it“ е невъзможно.

title: -ING vs -ED Adjectives
rule_en: -ING adjectives describe the thing that causes the feeling: a boring meeting. -ED adjectives describe how a person feels: I was bored. The meeting is interesting; I am interested.
rule_bg: Прилагателните на -ING описват нещото, което предизвиква усещането: a boring meeting. Прилагателните на -ED описват как се чувства човекът: I was bored. Срещата е interesting; аз съм interested.

form.label: -ing = the cause
form.value: The film is boring · the news is surprising

form.label: -ed = the person
form.value: I am bored · I was surprised

examples.en: The presentation was boring, so I felt bored.
examples.bg: Презентацията беше скучна, затова се отегчих.

examples.en: I'm interested in the offer, it looks interesting.
examples.bg: Заинтересован съм от офертата, изглежда интересна.

examples.en: The result was surprising; everyone was surprised.
examples.bg: Резултатът беше изненадващ; всички бяха изненадани.

exercises.sentence: The film was really ___.
exercises.why: -ing describes the thing that causes the feeling. The film is what causes the boredom.
exercises.why_bg: -ing описва нещото, което предизвиква чувството. Филмът предизвиква скуката.

exercises.sentence: I was ___ by the news.
exercises.why: -ed describes the person who feels it.
exercises.why_bg: -ed описва човека, който изпитва чувството.

exercises.sentence: This course is very ___.
exercises.why: The course causes the interest, so -ing. 'I am interesting' says that you are an interesting person.
exercises.why_bg: Курсът предизвиква интереса, значи -ing. „I am interesting“ значи, че ти си интересен човек.

exercises.sentence: She felt ___ after the long flight.
exercises.why: She is the one feeling it, so -ed.
exercises.why_bg: Тя е тази, която го изпитва, значи -ed.

exercises.sentence: The results were ___ for the whole team.
exercises.why: The results cause the excitement. The team would be excited.
exercises.why_bg: Резултатите предизвикват вълнението. Екипът би бил „excited“.

title: Words That Trick Bulgarian Speakers
rule_en: Some English words look like Bulgarian words but mean something different. "Actual" means real, not настоящ. "Eventually" means in the end, not евентуално. "Sympathetic" means understanding, not симпатичен. "Control" means to have power over something, not проверявам.
rule_bg: Някои английски думи изглеждат като български, но значат друго. „Actual“ значи действителен, не „настоящ“. „Eventually“ значи в крайна сметка, не „евентуално“. „Sympathetic“ значи състрадателен, не „симпатичен“. „Control“ значи управлявам, не „проверявам“.

examples.en: What is the current situation?
examples.bg: Не „actual situation“, когато имаш предвид настоящото положение.

examples.en: We will possibly need a second office.
examples.bg: Не „eventually“, когато имаш предвид „евентуално“.

examples.en: Please check the numbers before sending.
examples.bg: Не „control“, когато имаш предвид „провери“.

exercises.sentence: What is the ___ price, not the old one?
exercises.why: 'Actual' in English means real or true. For 'актуален' use current.
exercises.why_bg: „Actual“ на английски значи реален, истински. За „актуален“ ползвай „current“.

exercises.sentence: We might ___ need more staff.
exercises.why: 'Eventually' means in the end, after some time. For 'евентуално' use possibly or perhaps.
exercises.why_bg: „Eventually“ значи в крайна сметка, след време. За „евентуално“ ползвай „possibly“ или „perhaps“.

exercises.sentence: She's a very ___ colleague, easy to like.
exercises.why: 'Sympathetic' means showing understanding for someone's trouble. For 'симпатичен' use likeable or nice.
exercises.why_bg: „Sympathetic“ значи съчувстващ. За „симпатичен“ ползвай „likeable“ или „nice“.

exercises.sentence: Please ___ the numbers before sending.
exercises.why: 'Control' means to have power over something. For 'проверявам' use check.
exercises.why_bg: „Control“ значи контролирам, управлявам. За „проверявам“ ползвай „check“.

exercises.sentence: We ___ the project in six months.
exercises.why: 'Realize' means to understand something suddenly. For 'реализирам' use complete or carry out.
exercises.why_bg: „Realize“ значи осъзнавам. За „реализирам“ ползвай „complete“ или „carry out“.

title: MUCH, MANY and A LOT OF
rule_en: 'Many' goes with things you can count: many emails, many people. 'Much' goes with things you cannot: much time, much money. 'A lot of' works with both and sounds natural anywhere. In positive sentences 'much' sounds odd on its own, so 'I have a lot of work' beats 'I have much work'.
rule_bg: „Many“ върви с броими неща: many emails, many people. „Much“ с неброими: much time, much money. „A lot of“ върви и с двете и звучи естествено навсякъде. В положителни изречения самостоятелното „much“ звучи странно, затова „I have a lot of work“ е по-добре от „I have much work“.

form.label: many + countable
form.value: many emails · many people

form.label: much + uncountable
form.value: much time · much money

form.label: a lot of + both
form.value: a lot of work · a lot of questions

form.label: questions
form.value: How many people? · How much does it cost?

examples.en: I don't have much time, but I have a lot of questions.
examples.bg: Нямам много време, но имам много въпроси.

examples.en: How many people are coming? And how much does it cost?
examples.bg: Колко души идват? И колко струва?

examples.en: There isn't much information on their website.
examples.bg: На сайта им няма много информация.

exercises.sentence: How ___ emails did you get?
exercises.why: Emails can be counted, so 'many'.
exercises.why_bg: Имейлите се броят, значи „many“.

exercises.sentence: I don't have ___ time today.
exercises.why: Time is uncountable, so 'much'.
exercises.why_bg: Времето е неброимо, значи „much“.

exercises.sentence: She has ___ experience in sales.
exercises.why: 'Experience' is uncountable here, so 'many' is impossible. 'A lot of' fits.
exercises.why_bg: „Experience“ тук е неброимо, значи „many“ е невъзможно. „A lot of“ пасва.

exercises.sentence: How ___ does the licence cost?
exercises.why: Money is uncountable, so a price is asked with 'how much'.
exercises.why_bg: Парите са неброими, затова цената се пита с „how much“.

exercises.sentence: There are ___ people in the meeting room.
exercises.why: People are countable, and 'much' never goes with countable nouns.
exercises.why_bg: Хората са броими, а „much“ никога не върви с броими съществителни.

title: Countable vs Uncountable Nouns
rule_en: Information, advice, news, and furniture have no plural in English, even though their Bulgarian equivalents do. Say "a piece of advice", not "an advice". News and police also take special verb forms: the news IS good; the police ARE investigating.
rule_bg: Information, advice, news и furniture нямат множествено число на английски, макар че на български имат. Казва се „a piece of advice“, не „an advice“. News и police вървят с особени глаголни форми: the news IS good; the police ARE investigating.

form.label: countable
form.value: a report · two reports · How many?

form.label: uncountable
form.value: information · advice · news · furniture · How much?

form.label: counting the uncountable
form.value: a piece of advice · two pieces of information

form.label: odd ones
form.value: news is (singular) · police are (plural)

examples.en: I need more information, not more informations.
examples.bg: Трябва ми повече информация, без множествено число.

examples.en: Thanks for the advice.
examples.bg: Благодаря за съвета.

examples.en: The news is good today.
examples.bg: Новината е добра днес.

exercises.sentence: I need more ___.
exercises.why: 'Information' is uncountable in English and has no plural. To count it, say 'a piece of information'.
exercises.why_bg: „Information“ е неброимо и няма множествено число. За броене: „a piece of information“.

exercises.sentence: Can I give you a piece of ___?
exercises.why: 'Advice' is uncountable too. The countable unit is 'a piece of advice'.
exercises.why_bg: „Advice“ също е неброимо. Броимата единица е „a piece of advice“.

exercises.sentence: The news ___ very good.
exercises.why: 'News' looks plural because of the -s, but it takes a singular verb.
exercises.why_bg: „News“ изглежда множествено заради -s, но иска глагол в единствено число.

exercises.sentence: We bought new ___ for the office.
exercises.why: 'Furniture' is uncountable. Count it with 'pieces of furniture', or name the items.
exercises.why_bg: „Furniture“ е неброимо. Брои се с „pieces of furniture“ или изброяваш предметите.

exercises.sentence: The police ___ investigating the case.
exercises.why: 'Police' always takes a plural verb in English, even though it is one organisation.
exercises.why_bg: „Police“ винаги иска глагол в множествено число, макар да е една организация.

title: SOME, ANY, A FEW and A LITTLE
rule_en: 'Some' goes in positive sentences and in offers: 'I have some questions', 'Would you like some coffee?'. 'Any' goes in negatives and most questions: 'I don't have any time', 'Do you have any questions?'. 'A few' is for countable things and 'a little' for uncountable: a few emails, a little time. Drop the 'a' and the meaning turns negative: 'few people came' means almost nobody.
rule_bg: „Some“ в положителни изречения и в предложения: „I have some questions“, „Would you like some coffee?“. „Any“ в отрицания и повечето въпроси: „I don't have any time“, „Do you have any questions?“. „A few“ за броими неща, „a little“ за неброими: a few emails, a little time. Махнеш ли „a“, значението става отрицателно: „few people came“ значи почти никой.

form.label: some
form.value: positive sentences and offers

form.label: any
form.value: negatives and most questions

form.label: a few + countable
form.value: a few emails · a few people

form.label: a little + uncountable
form.value: a little time · a little money

form.label: without a
form.value: few people = almost nobody

examples.en: I have some good news and a few questions.
examples.bg: Имам добри новини и няколко въпроса.

examples.en: We don't have any information yet.
examples.bg: Още нямаме никаква информация.

examples.en: Give me a little time and I'll have an answer.
examples.bg: Дай ми малко време и ще имам отговор.

exercises.sentence: I don't have ___ time today.
exercises.why: A negative sentence takes 'any'.
exercises.why_bg: Отрицателно изречение иска „any“.

exercises.sentence: Would you like ___ coffee?
exercises.why: Offers take 'some', even though they are questions.
exercises.why_bg: Предложенията са със „some“, макар да са въпроси.

exercises.sentence: I've got ___ emails to answer.
exercises.why: Emails are countable, so 'a few'.
exercises.why_bg: Имейлите са броими, значи „a few“.

exercises.sentence: We have ___ money left in the budget.
exercises.why: Money is uncountable, so 'a little'.
exercises.why_bg: Парите са неброими, значи „a little“.

exercises.sentence: ___ people came, so we cancelled.
exercises.why: Without 'a', 'few' means almost none. 'A few' would have meant enough to continue.
exercises.why_bg: Без „a“, „few“ значи почти никой. „A few“ би значело достатъчно, за да продължим.

title: Comparatives and Superlatives
rule_en: Don't double the comparative or superlative. "Better" is already comparative — never "more better". "Best" is already superlative — never "most best". Don't put "very much" before an adjective; just use "very".
rule_bg: Не удвоявай сравнителната или превъзходната степен. „Better“ вече е сравнителна степен — никога „more better“. „Best“ вече е превъзходна степен — никога „most best“. Пред прилагателно не се слага „very much“, само „very“.

form.label: short adjectives
form.value: tall → taller → the tallest

form.label: long adjectives
form.value: expensive → more expensive → the most expensive

form.label: irregular
form.value: good → better → best · bad → worse → worst

form.label: never
form.value: more better · most best · very much interesting

examples.en: This solution is better, not more better.
examples.bg: Това решение е по-добро, не „more better“.

examples.en: It was the best result, not the most best.
examples.bg: Беше най-добрият резултат, не „most best“.

examples.en: The report is very interesting, not very much interesting.
examples.bg: Докладът е много интересен, не „very much interesting“.

exercises.sentence: This offer is ___ than the last one.
exercises.why: 'Better' is already a comparative. Never put 'more' in front of it.
exercises.why_bg: „Better“ вече е сравнителна степен. Никога не се слага „more“ пред нея.

exercises.sentence: It was the ___ result of the year.
exercises.why: 'Best' is already a superlative. 'Most best' says it twice.
exercises.why_bg: „Best“ вече е превъзходна степен. „Most best“ го казва два пъти.

exercises.sentence: The plan is ___ interesting.
exercises.why: 'Very much' doesn't stand in front of an adjective. Either 'very interesting' or 'much more interesting'.
exercises.why_bg: „Very much“ не стои пред прилагателно. Или „very interesting“, или „much more interesting“.

exercises.sentence: She's ___ than her brother.
exercises.why: Short adjectives take -er rather than 'more'. Tall, taller, tallest.
exercises.why_bg: Късите прилагателни взимат -er, не „more“. Tall, taller, tallest.

exercises.sentence: That was the ___ meeting we've ever had.
exercises.why: 'Worst' is the superlative of 'bad' and needs no 'most'.
exercises.why_bg: „Worst“ е превъзходната степен на „bad“ и не иска „most“.

title: AS ... AS and Other Comparison Patterns
rule_en: 'As ... as' says two things are equal: 'This offer is as good as the last one'. The negative says they are not: 'It isn't as expensive as I thought'. Use 'the same as' for identical things, and 'different from' rather than 'different than'. To show how big the difference is, add much, far or a bit: 'much better', 'a bit cheaper'.
rule_bg: „As ... as“ казва, че две неща са равни: „This offer is as good as the last one“. Отрицанието казва, че не са: „It isn't as expensive as I thought“. „The same as“ за еднакви неща, а „different from“, не „different than“. За да покажеш колко голяма е разликата, добавяш much, far или a bit: „much better“, „a bit cheaper“.

form.label: equal
form.value: as good as · as expensive as

form.label: not equal
form.value: not as expensive as I thought

form.label: identical
form.value: the same as (never the same like)

form.label: different
form.value: different from (not different than)

form.label: size of the gap
form.value: much better · far cheaper · a bit slower

examples.en: This supplier is as reliable as the old one, and a bit cheaper.
examples.bg: Този доставчик е толкова надежден, колкото стария, и малко по-евтин.

examples.en: It wasn't as difficult as we expected.
examples.bg: Не беше толкова трудно, колкото очаквахме.

examples.en: Their offer is the same as ours, but the delivery time is different from theirs.
examples.bg: Офертата им е същата като нашата, но срокът на доставка е различен от техния.

exercises.sentence: This year was ___ good as last year.
exercises.why: The pattern is as + adjective + as.
exercises.why_bg: Моделът е as + прилагателно + as.

exercises.sentence: It isn't ___ expensive as I thought.
exercises.why: The negative keeps the same 'as ... as' frame.
exercises.why_bg: Отрицанието запазва същата рамка „as ... as“.

exercises.sentence: Their price is the same ___ ours.
exercises.why: 'The same as' is fixed. 'The same like' does not exist.
exercises.why_bg: „The same as“ е устойчиво. „The same like“ не съществува.

exercises.sentence: This version is different ___ the one you sent.
exercises.why: 'Different from' is the standard. 'Different than' appears in American English and is safer avoided.
exercises.why_bg: „Different from“ е стандартът. „Different than“ се среща в американски английски и е по-добре да се избягва.

exercises.sentence: The new system is ___ faster than the old one.
exercises.why: 'Very' doesn't go with a comparative. Use much, far or a lot.
exercises.why_bg: „Very“ не върви със сравнителна степен. Ползва се much, far или a lot.

title: Common Word Partners (Collocations)
rule_en: Some words always go together, and the pair often doesn't translate directly. Prices are HIGH or LOW, not big or small. You MAKE a mistake but DO your homework. You TAKE a photo and TAKE an exam. Lights are TURNED ON and OFF.
rule_bg: Някои думи винаги вървят заедно и двойката често не се превежда буквално. Цените са HIGH или LOW, не big/small. Грешка се „прави“ с MAKE, но домашно с DO. Снимка и изпит се „вземат“ с TAKE. Лампите се TURN ON/OFF.

examples.en: The price is too high, not too big.
examples.bg: Цената е твърде висока, не „big“.

examples.en: I made a mistake in the invoice.
examples.bg: Направих грешка във фактурата.

examples.en: Can you take a photo of the whiteboard?
examples.bg: Можеш ли да снимаш дъската?

exercises.sentence: The price is very ___ this month.
exercises.why: Prices are high or low in English, never big or small.
exercises.why_bg: Цените на английски са high или low, никога big или small.

exercises.sentence: I ___ a mistake in the report.
exercises.why: You make a mistake and you do your homework. The pairing is fixed and there is no rule behind it.
exercises.why_bg: Прави се „make a mistake“ и „do homework“. Двойката е устойчива и няма правило зад нея.

exercises.sentence: She ___ her homework every evening.
exercises.why: Homework, housework and the washing-up all take 'do'.
exercises.why_bg: „Homework“, „housework“ и миенето на чинии са с „do“.

exercises.sentence: Can you ___ a photo of this?
exercises.why: In English you take a photo. 'Make a photo' is a translation of 'правя снимка'.
exercises.why_bg: На английски снимката се „take“. „Make a photo“ е превод на „правя снимка“.

exercises.sentence: Please ___ off the light when you leave.
exercises.why: Lights are turned on and off, never opened and closed.
exercises.why_bg: Лампите се „turn on“ и „turn off“, никога „open“ и „close“.

title: Subject-Verb Agreement
rule_en: "Everybody", "everyone" and "nobody" take a singular verb: everybody IS ready. In business English, collective nouns like "team" and "company" are usually singular too: our team IS working on it.
rule_bg: „Everybody“, „everyone“ и „nobody“ вървят с глагол в единствено число: everybody IS ready. В бизнес английски „team“ и „company“ също обикновено са в единствено число: our team IS working on it.

form.label: singular verb
form.value: everybody is · nobody knows · everyone has

form.label: one organisation
form.value: the company is · our team is

form.label: always plural
form.value: the police are

form.label: looks plural, is singular
form.value: the news is

examples.en: Everybody is ready for the call.
examples.bg: Всички са готови за разговора.

examples.en: Our team is working on it.
examples.bg: Нашият екип работи по въпроса.

examples.en: Nobody knows the answer yet.
examples.bg: Никой още не знае отговора.

exercises.sentence: Everybody ___ ready for the meeting.
exercises.why: 'Everybody' and 'everyone' look plural but take a singular verb.
exercises.why_bg: „Everybody“ и „everyone“ изглеждат множествено, но искат глагол в единствено число.

exercises.sentence: Our team ___ finishing the project this week.
exercises.why: British English allows 'are' when you mean the individuals, but in writing 'is' is safer: the team acts as one.
exercises.why_bg: Британският английски допуска „are“, когато имаш предвид хората поотделно, но в писане „is“ е по-безопасно: екипът действа като едно цяло.

exercises.sentence: Nobody ___ the password.
exercises.why: 'Nobody' is singular, exactly like 'everybody'.
exercises.why_bg: „Nobody“ е в единствено число, точно като „everybody“.

exercises.sentence: The company ___ growing fast.
exercises.why: A company is one thing, so it takes a singular verb.
exercises.why_bg: Компанията е едно нещо, значи глагол в единствено число.

exercises.sentence: Everyone ___ their own opinion.
exercises.why: 'Everyone' takes a singular verb even though 'their' follows it. That mix is normal English.
exercises.why_bg: „Everyone“ иска глагол в единствено число, макар след него да идва „their“. Тази смес е нормален английски.

title: Don't Translate Word for Word
rule_en: Some Bulgarian sentence patterns don't translate directly. Age uses "be", not "have": I AM 30, not I have 30 years. "Thank God" has no "s". For progress up to now, say "so far", not "till now".
rule_bg: Някои български изречения не се превеждат буквално. Възрастта е с „be“, не с „have“: I AM 30. „Thank God“ е без „s“. За напредък досега казваме „so far“, не „till now“.

examples.en: I am 30 years old.
examples.bg: На 30 години съм.

examples.en: Thank God it's Friday.
examples.bg: Слава Богу, петък е.

examples.en: So far we have three applications.
examples.bg: Досега имаме три кандидатури.

exercises.sentence: I ___ 30 years old.
exercises.why: Age uses 'be' in English: I am 30. 'I have 30 years' is the Bulgarian structure.
exercises.why_bg: Възрастта е с „be“: I am 30. „I have 30 years“ е българската конструкция.

exercises.sentence: ___ God it's Friday!
exercises.why: The phrase is 'Thank God', with the verb. 'Thanks God' adds an -s that doesn't belong there.
exercises.why_bg: Изразът е „Thank God“, с глагола. „Thanks God“ добавя -s, което няма място там.

exercises.sentence: ___, we have three confirmed bookings.
exercises.why: 'So far' means up to this moment. 'Till now' is a literal translation of 'досега' and sounds wrong.
exercises.why_bg: „So far“ значи до този момент. „Till now“ е буквален превод на „досега“ и звучи грешно.

exercises.sentence: My sister ___ 25 years old.
exercises.why: Same rule as your own age: people are 25, they don't have 25.
exercises.why_bg: Същото правило като за твоята възраст: хората „are 25“, не „have 25“.

exercises.sentence: I ___ a car today, so I can give you a lift.
exercises.why: 'I have a car' says you own one or have it with you. 'I am with a car' is the Bulgarian 'с кола съм'.
exercises.why_bg: „I have a car“ значи, че имаш кола или е с теб. „I am with a car“ е българското „с кола съм“.
